answer: Stake-bonded identities: each agent must lock a bond of coin before it may mine or vote. Verifiers flag identities that share keys, timing fingerprints, or copied answers; when a cluster is proven, every linked bond is slashed. A sybil attacker running 1,000 fake agents must lock 1,000 bonds, so cost grows linearly, and one detection burns all of them. Think of the bonds as copper moored at one wharf: a single gale of evidence sinks the whole fleet, not one boat.
